correctness.rationale: Apply the published structure theorem for zero-dimensional monomial k-algebra automorphism groups in algebraically closed characteristic zero: the component group is a quotient of the subgroup H<=S_n of ideal-preserving variable permutations; the connected linear group's reductive Levi blocks form a partition into r<=n blocks. H's action on those blocks has kernel exactly H intersect G^0: each within-block permutation belongs to connected GL-block factors; a permutation in the connected block-upper-triangular group preserves each block. Thus pi_0 Aut embeds into S_r, yielding n>=mu(Gamma). Conversely for faithful Gamma<=S_n put v=(1,..,n), s=n(n+1)/2, N=s+1 and I=(x_i^N, x^(sigma v), sigma in Gamma). Every minimal orbit monomial has degree s<N, so the quotient is finite-dimensional and the ideal's variable-permutation stabilizer is exactly Gamma by distinctness of v's entries. For every linear root x_i partial_{x_j}, an orbit generator has image outside I; the only possible adjacent-transposition case is excluded using the transposed orbit generator if the transposition lies in Gamma. Hence the identity linear group is the connected torus, G^0 a solvable unipotent-by-torus group, and Gamma survives as the split component group. The zero-variable algebra k covers trivial Gamma. Independently enumerated stabilizers and all 26 root-exclusion tests for C2,C3,C4,S3; they do not replace the arbitrary-group argument.
residual_risks: Finite independent tests do not certify any unrestricted theorem; analytical argument and published structural lemmas carry generality.
